learning_outcomes.text: Students know the fundamental concepts of system software.
Students can handle Unix operating system commands.
Students know the methods of computer communication.
Students know the concepts of the Internet.
Students can follow scientific working methods (recognizing, formulating, solving problems, training abstraction skills).
Students are able to speak freely about scientific content, both in front of an audience and in a discussion.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of system software: tasks, processes, resource management, synchronization, deadlocks, memory management, file systems, input/output, virtualization, Unix introduction
Fundamentals of computer communication: Protocols: ISO-OSI, TCP/IP
Data transfer: Twisted Pair, Coax, Fiber optics, Bit encodings, Modulation techniques
Networks: LANs, WANs, GANs, MANs, Ethernet, Token Ring, Bridges, Routers, FDDI, ATM
Internet: TCP/UDP/IP Protocols, Internet addresses, Routing, DNS, ARP, FTP, E-Mail, HTTP, WWW

assessment_methods.method: Weekly exercises (at least 50% of points and oral presentation of at least two solutions)

assessment_rules: To acquire credits, students must achieve at least 50 percent of the points from the weekly exercises and orally present the solution to at least two of the exercise tasks. The final grade is based on a written exam, graded from 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the B.Sc. Computer Science program.
